hypothesis: Paired N=256 arm (seeds 56, 57, 58, 62, 63, otherwise identical to the 5-step N=64 arm). Across 11 matched seeds, the half-final-margin delay (N=256 minus N=64) was +10 or more in every seed, mean about +31. The 0.1-bar delay ranged from 0 to +70. At matched 5-step resolution in both arms, accel_step reaches half of its own final margin later at N=256 than at N=64 for the same seed. The half-final measure is the more stable timing statistic. All steps are read from the per-checkpoint trajectories of both arms.
expected_if_true: The half-final delay is >= +15 in at least 4 of 5 matched seeds, and its mean over the 5 seeds is >= +20. The 0.1-bar persistent delay has a larger seed-to-seed spread (range wider than the half-final range). Final accel_step margin is >= 0.1 at N=256 in all seeds, and val_mse_ratio stays above 1.
expected_if_false: The half-final delay is <= +10 in at least 3 of 5 matched seeds, or its 5-seed mean is < +10. That would mean the earlier delay came from mixed checkpoint spacing or seed selection and does not reflect a steps_per_orbit effect.
